steps.body: Whole numbers are fractions too: 8/4 means eight fourths, and every four of them rebuild one whole, so 8/4 is exactly 2.
steps.narration: Whole numbers are fractions too: 8/4 means eight fourths, and every four of them rebuild one whole, so 8/4 is exactly 2.

widget.prompt: Build 6/3 and see how many wholes it makes.
widget.successFeedback: 6/3 — six thirds, and every three of them make a whole, so this is exactly 2.
widget.lowFeedback: Your shaded bar is shorter than the target half. Shade more — raise the numerator, or use fewer parts.
widget.highFeedback: Your shaded bar is longer than half. Shade less — lower the numerator, or split into more parts.

commonFractions.feedback: 1/3 is a single piece; six of them were asked for.
3/6 is half of one whole — the numbers were swapped.

predict.reveal: Four fourths rebuild one whole, and eight fourths contain two such groups.

cml.actionGoal: Cut, count, and compare equal pieces to see what g3f whole as fraction really names.
invariants: A fraction names equal shares of ONE whole: the denominator says how many equal pieces the whole became, and the numerator counts them, which is what makes g3f whole as fraction comparable at all.
misconceptions: Calling unequal pieces fractions, reading the denominator as a count, or comparing fractions that came from different-sized wholes.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the whole changed size, which of these comparisons would stop being trustworthy?

widget.prompt: Convert 8/2 to a mixed number. What is the WHOLE NUMBER part?

commonErrors.feedback: 8 counts the PIECES. Every 2 of them rebuild one whole, so ask how many groups of 2 fit.
2 is the piece size, not how many wholes 8 pieces make.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Name the equal pieces the whole was cut into, then count how many of them the question is about.

widget.prompt: Compute 2 × 1/4 as ?/4. What is the numerator?

commonErrors.feedback: 4 is the DENOMINATOR — it names the piece size and never changes when you collect pieces.
Adding the two numbers mixes a count of pieces with a piece size; only the count grows.
